rows.t: Hermes of the golden wand — an honored guest, and a rare one. Sit, and let me set ambrosia and red nectar before you. What errand brings you across so much salt water? Speak it; my heart says do it, if it can be done.

rows.t: You ask, goddess, and I answer truly: Zeus sent me — who would cross this waste of brine for pleasure? He says you keep here the most ill-fated of all the men who fought at Troy, and that it is not his doom to die far from his people. Send him quickly, and do not wake the Thunderer's anger against you.

rows.t: Unhappy man, weep here no longer — I am ready now to let you go. Rise; cut long timbers and build yourself a broad raft, and I will stock her with bread and water and red wine, and send a fair wind behind you for home.

And if some god wrecks me again on the wine-dark water, I will endure that too — my heart is old in suffering.

rows.t: Your veil, goddess — with my life for thanks.
